facts.text: Primghar’s name comes from the first letters of eight early settlers—Pumphrey, Roberts, Inman, McCormack, Green, Hayes, Albright, and Rerick—plotted the town in 1872.
In 1873, a countywide vote moved the courthouse to the exact center of O’Brien County, and the current courthouse was finished in 1917.
Tjossem Park, a former rock quarry donated by the Tjossem family in 1989, now offers fishing and picnicking just a mile south‑southeast of Primghar.
Primghar sits at 1,520 feet above sea level, overlooking gently rolling northwest Iowa farmland.
The town’s soil is silty clay loam, with glacial till reaching 30 to 60 inches deep—typical of the region’s fertile yet erosion‑prone landscape.
